title: Symmetry and Parity of an Odd Polynomial g(x) = x^3 + x
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Test the function g(x) = x^3 + x algebraically to determine whether it is even, odd, or neither, and justify your conclusion.

steps.title: Evaluate the Function at -x
steps.explanation: Substitute -x into every instance of the independent variable x in the definition of g(x).
steps.why: Testing for function parity requires evaluating the response of the formula to a negated input.

steps.title: Simplify Using Odd Power Rules
steps.explanation: Because 3 and 1 are odd exponents, (-x)^3 = -x^3 and (-x)^1 = -x.
steps.why: Odd integer powers preserve the negative sign: (-x)^n = -x^n for odd integers n.

steps.title: Factor Out -1 and Conclude
steps.explanation: Factoring -1 from both terms shows that g(-x) = -g(x) for all real numbers x, so g is an odd function.
steps.why: The sum of two odd functions (x^3 and x) is always an odd function.
